data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (read) caused by unchecked pointer advancement past end of buffer
data.rationale: Reached via magic_buffer -> file_buffer -> file_is_json -> json_parse -> json_parse_array -> json_parse. In json_parse_const (is_json.c:329) the output pointer is advanced unconditionally: *ucp += --len - 1; with no check that enough bytes remain before ue. It also returns 1 (success) even when the loop terminates early because uc hit ue, so a truncated constant such as 'f' inside '[f' is reported as successfully parsed while the caller's cursor was pushed 4 bytes past the buffer end. Back in json_parse_array, the uc == ue guard (line 193) is false because uc > ue, so the switch (*uc) at line 195 reads out of bounds. ASan confirms: 2-byte input '[f' gives heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at json_parse_array is_json.c:195 called from json_parse is_json.c:370 and file_is_json is_json.c:431. The fix is to bounds-check the remaining constant length (uc + len > ue) before advancing and only return success if the whole constant matched.
